commands.author: VectorPeak

target.title: fix(discord): split encoded video URLs from captions
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Discord outbound send edge case where a caption + video URL can miss the existing caption-first/media-second split when the URL encodes the extension dot, such as `render%2Emp4`.

The split decision depends on Discord's local video URL classification. `new URL(...).pathname` preserves `%2E`, so a path like `/attachments/1/render%2Emp4` did not match the existing `.mp4` / `.webm` / `.mov` suffix check and was treated as non-video.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production change is intentionally small and stays inside Discord's local media detector:

```diff
 const parsed = new URL(trimmed);
-return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+try {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(decodeURIComponent(parsed.pathname));
+} catch {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+}
```

This decodes URL pathnames before video-extension matching, while preserving the previous fallback for malformed percent encoding. Local non-URL paths still use the existing query/hash stripping path, and the original `mediaUrl` is still passed through to the Discord send call.

## User Impact

Discord outbound sends with a caption and an encoded video extension now follow the same behavior covered by the existing video split path: the caption text is sent first, then the video media is sent separately.

For example, `https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1` now classifies like a normal `.mp4` URL for the Discord caption/video split decision.

## Evidence

Local validation:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 48 tests.

Runtime outbound-path proof:

This proof imports the real Discord outbound adapter and calls `discordOutbound.sendMedia` with the encoded-dot video URL. The only injected part is the final Discord send transport, so the transcript can observe whether the production outbound adapter chooses one combined send or the caption-first/media-second split.

```text
[proof] Discord outbound production adapter with injected Discord send transport
[proof] input mediaUrl=https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
[proof] send call count=2
[proof] call 1: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"rendered clip","mediaUrl":null,"reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] call 2: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"","mediaUrl":"https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1","reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] returned={"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"redacted-discord-channel"}
[proof] PASS: encoded-dot video URL takes caption-first/media-second outbound path
```

Stronger local send-stack proof:

I also exercised the adapter through the real `sendMessageDiscord` media path and captured the final Discord REST request bodies before the network boundary. This uses an encoded `file://.../render%2Emp4` URL because local loopback HTTP is correctly blocked by the repo's SSRF guard; `file://` still goes through the same `new URL(...).pathname` encoded-dot branch that this PR fixes, then lets the real media loader read the decoded `render.mp4` and lets the real send runtime build the Discord upload body.

```text
[proof] Discord encoded file URL + real send runtime
[proof] input mediaUrl=file:///C:/Users/MiaoXing/AppData/Local/Temp/openclaw-discord-proof-OkZVLJ/render%2Emp4
[proof] decoded media path read=["C:\\Users\\MiaoXing\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\openclaw-discord-proof-OkZVLJ\\render.mp4"]
[proof] Discord REST calls=2
[proof] REST call 1: {"route":"/channels/789/messages","content":"rendered clip","files":[]}
[proof] REST call 2: {"route":"/channels/789/messages","content":"","files":[{"name":"render.mp4","size":24}]}
[proof] returned={"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"789","receipt":{"primaryPlatformMessageId":"proof-2","platformMessageIds":["proof-2"],"parts":[{"platformMessageId":"proof-2","kind":"media","index":0,"raw":{"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"789"}}],"sentAt":1783481407554,"raw":[{"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"789"}]}}
[proof] PASS: encoded-dot file URL takes caption-first/media-second path and real media send uploads render.mp4
```

Focused behavior covered by the regression test:

```text
mediaUrl = https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
caption send -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "rendered clip", ...)
media send   -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "", { mediaUrl })
```

Call chain / impact:

```text
discordOutbound captioned media send
-> normalizeMediaPathForExtension(mediaUrl)
-> URL pathname extraction
-> video extension check
-> caption/media split decision
```

Scope and sibling surfaces:

- Production diff is limited to `extensions/discord/src/media-detection.ts` and changes only URL pathname normalization before suffix detection.
- The test change extends the existing Discord outbound split test in `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` instead of adding a new broad test surface.
- No shared media-core helper is changed; this PR intentionally scopes the fix to Discord's local caption/video split detector.
- Malformed percent encoding still falls back to the original URL pathname, so this does not add a new send-time exception path.

Live-proof note:

- This local environment does not expose Discord live smoke credentials (`DISCORD_*` / `OPENCLAW_*DISCORD*` env vars were absent), and the repository's Discord live QA workflow requires maintainer-level repository access. The terminal proofs above exercise the production outbound decision path and the local real send-stack body construction path, while avoiding any claim of live Discord network delivery.
